content: Preact (MIT) ~3-4KB gzipped runtime, React-compatible API, minimal component overhead -- best fit for small admin-style SPA replacing htmx. Svelte (MIT) compiles away framework at build time (~2-7KB per app) but is a different authoring paradigm (no runtime vdom) with a required compiler step. Vue 3 (MIT) is heavier (~22KB) with more built-in conventions (SFC, reactivity system) -- more than needed for a config/chooser UI. Vite (MIT) is the standard build tool for all three, outputs static JS/CSS/HTML bundles that can be copied into any static-file host at build time; no runtime CDN dependency once built -- CDN-free/air-gapped is achievable with any of the three as long as the build output is committed/baked into the image rather than fetched from a CDN at runtime.
